subject: English
passage: "Evening in October" is a 2004 poem by Rania Toure. In the poem, the speaker describes having contradictory feelings while walking through a park on an autumn evening: ______
prompt: Which quotation from "Evening in October" most effectively illustrates the claim?

choices.A: "The amber leaves came spiraling down / Past lamp-lit boughs and garden gate; / And every one that touched the ground / Seemed glad to meet its fate."
choices.B: "The crisp air turned my breath to plume, / I watched it rise and disappear; / And I resolved, despite the gloom, / To find some beauty here."
choices.C: "A robin paused upon the stone / And cocked its head as if to say / Some word I could not name or own, / Yet felt was kind that day."
choices.D: "I walked beneath the reddened trees / Where laughter from the playground came, / And strange it was that sounds of ease / Should wake an older ache the same."

explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it most effectively illustrates the claim that the speaker has contradictory feelings while experiencing the sights and sounds of an autumn evening. This quotation indicates that the speaker is walking beneath autumn trees and hearing laughter from a nearby playground. Even though these sounds are described as "sounds of ease," they simultaneously "wake an older ache" in the speaker. In other words, these lines illustrate the claim that the speaker experiences contradictory feelings—pleasant sounds producing an aching response—while immersed in the sights and sounds of the season.
